Though the matter is listed for hearing on interlocutory application, with the consent of the learned counsel for the petitioners,
it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This petition is filed by accused No.1 under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 20231 with prayer to following relief;
a) The petitioner/accused No.1 preferring the criminal petition u/s 528 of BNSS to quash the entire proceedings in CC NO.299/2025 in crime No.48/2025 of Mudhol PS for the offence punishable under Section 115(2), 324(2), 329(4), 109(1), 352, 351(3) of BNS pending on the file of Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC Mudhol, District: Bagalkote against the petitioner/accused No.1 now committed to the I Additional District and Sessions Court Bagalkot sitting at Jamakhandi in the interest of justice.

Hereinafter referred to as "BNSS, 2023"
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3465 HC-KAR 3.
The case of the prosecution, in brief, is that the son of the complainant was residing in Dharwad for preparation for the KAS examination.

During that time, the petitioner developed a friendship Pratiba D/O Siddarth Dulari vs State Of Karnataka on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38093115/
2 with son the complainant namely Mahantesh.

entities.text: Pratiba D/O Siddarth Dulari vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner came to the house of the complainant and informed her that the complainant's son was in love with her and requested that their marriage be performed.
At that moment, the son of the complainant refused to marry her.

The petitioner,
being annoyed by this, developed enmity against the complainant and her son Mahantesh.
4. On 18.02.2025, when Mahantesh was sleeping inside his house, the petitioner allegedly trespassed into the house of the complainant and asked the son of the complainant to marry her.
An altercation ensued, during which she took a sickle and tried to assault the son of the complainant.
She also threw stones at the complainant's house, broke the window, and caused damage to the house.
Therefore, based on these allegations, the complaint was NC: 2026:KHC-D:3465 HC-KAR registered against the petitioner for the above stated offences.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the present complaint has been filed as a counterblast to the earlier complaint lodged by the petitioner, which is registered in Crime No.289/2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 417, 376, 504, and 506 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(w), 3(1)(i), 3(2)(v-a), and 3(2)(a) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 19892.
Therefore, the complainant has filed a false case to harass the petitioner.
Hence, it is an abuse of the process of the Court, and he prays to allow the petition.

6. On the other hand, the learned HCGP for the State submitted that this is not a counter case and that ample material is available in the case; therefore, the prosecution has proceeded against the petitioner.
From the Hereinafter referred to as "SC and ST (POA) Act, 1989".
NC : 2026:KHC-D:3465 HC-KAR averments in the complaint, there are sufficient materials available to proceed with the trial.
There are no grounds to invoke Section 528 of BNSS, 2023.
(Section 482 of Cr.P.C)
Therefore, he prays to dismiss the petition.

7. Learned counsel for respondent No.2/complainant, reiterating the submissions made by the learned HCGP, further submitted that during the investigation it was revealed that the petitioner herein trespassed into the house and threw stones at the windows, due to which the glass panes were broken.
There is prima facie material available during the course of investigation.

Therefore,
the petitioner has not made out any prima facie case, and hence the proceedings cannot be quashed.
Therefore, he prays for dismissal of the petition.

8. Upon considering the material available at this stage, including the complaint, FIR, and statements, it is seen that earlier the petitioner had lodged a complaint against Mahantesh for the offences punishable under Sections 417, 376, 504, and 506 of IPC and Sections NC:
2026:KHC-D:3465 HC-KAR 3(1)(w), 3(1)(i), 3(2)(v-a), and 3(2)(a) of the SC and ST, Act, 1989.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the present complaint is a counterblast to the earlier complaint; however, it cannot be prima facie concluded that the petitioner has made out such a case.
9. The averments in the complaint clearly state that on 18.02.2025 the petitioner trespassed into the house of the complainant and committed the offences as alleged in the complaint.

The allegation Pratiba D/O Siddarth Dulari vs State Of Karnataka on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38093115/
3 against the petitioner is that she took a sickle and tried to assault the complainant's son, who managed to escape.

entities.text: Pratiba D/O Siddarth Dulari vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the wound certificate, there may not be any mention of injuries caused by the assault, but that alone is not a ground to hold that there is no case for trial.
10. Further, the photographs of the complainant's house produced before the Court show signs of broken windows.
Therefore, there is sufficient material, and the prosecution has prima facie made out a case to proceed NC: 2026:KHC-D:3465 HC-KAR against the petitioner.
There is no abuse of the process of the law/Court.

11. Merely because in another case lodged by the petitioner a stay has been granted by this Court,
which was under different facts and circumstances pertaining to that case, the same cannot be made applicable to the present case so as to quash the proceedings.

Since this Court, at this stage, does not find any abuse of the process of law or Court, and as charges have already been framed and the trial has begun and the case is in the midst of trial, no case is made out to quash the proceedings against the petitioner.
12. Accordingly, the petition is liable to be dismissed, and it is dismissed.
In view of the dismissal of petition, pending I.A.'s, if any, shall also stands dismissed.

Sd/-
(HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR) JUDGE ASN /CT-AN
